questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Vague
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Indefinite**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"vague"** means something that is not clearly expressed, defined, or understood; it lacks clarity or precision. (अस्पष्ट)

 
 
• **Example: **Her instructions were so vague that no one knew exactly what to do.
 
 
 
• **"Indefinite" **refers to something that is not clearly defined, having no exact limits. (अनिश्चित)
 
 
• **Example: **The project has been postponed for an indefinite period due to unforeseen circumstances.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can conclude that the synonym of **'vague'** is **'indefinite'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Indefinite**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Dissimilar **(असमान): Not alike; different.

 
 
• **Example:** The two sisters are quite dissimilar in their personalities.
 
 
 
• **Distinct **(स्पष्ट): Clearly different or of a different kind.
 
 
• **Example: **There are two distinct types of people in the world.
 
 
 
• **Intact** (अखंडित): Not damaged or impaired in any way; complete.
 
 
• **Example:** The ancient vase remained intact despite its long journey.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He is the __healthy__ person I have ever met in life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' healthiest .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The superlative degree **"healthiest" **is correct here because the sentence compares the person to all others the speaker has met, implying that he is at the extreme of health among all.
 
• The structure **"the + superlative adjective"** is used when referring to the highest degree of a quality in a specific group.
 
• In a superlative sentence, the correct form of the **adjective **is usually formed by adding **"-est"** to the base form of the adjective.

Correct sentence: *He is the **healthiest** person I have ever met in life*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:**

 
 
• **Structure:** adjective + -er (or more + adjective for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example:** He is healthier than his brother.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare two people or things.
 
 
 
• **Positive Degree:**
 
 
• **Structure: **base form of the adjective.
 
• **Example: **He is a healthy person.
 
• **Usage: **Used to describe the quality of one person or thing without any comparison.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**like**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage talks about a quest for ancient things that could have a soul, and the phrase “something like Aladdin’s lamp” refers to an object that is similar in function to Aladdin's lamp.
 
• The word "**like**" is used to show **similarity**, indicating that the ancient things she sought were similar to Aladdin's lamp in possessing a soul.
 
• **"Of" **would typically indicate **possession**, which is not appropriate in this context. **"Upstairs" **refers to a location, and** "by"** indicates proximity, none of which fit the idea of similarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *She went on a quest for ancient things like__ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She __kept__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an __apothecary__ table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __wise__ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Of"** would indicate possession (e.g., "the lamp of Aladdin"), but the sentence refers to something similar to the lamp, not owned by it.
 
• **"Upstairs"** and **"by"** are more location-based prepositions and do not convey the idea of similarity in this context.
 
• **"Like"** is the best choice as it directly expresses the comparison between the ancient things and Aladdin's lamp.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**was**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage is written in the **past tense**, indicating actions that were ongoing at some point in the past.
 
• **"Was"** fits this past tense context, as it suggests something that happened in the past and continued for a while.
 
• **"Has been"** refers to an action that started in the past and continues into the present, which does not align with the context of this passage.
 
• **"Were" **is a past tense verb used with plural subjects or hypothetical situations, but the subject in this sentence is singular, so it does not fit.
 
• **"Is"** is present tense, but the passage discusses past events, so it would not be grammatically correct here.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *She went on a quest for ancient things that__ could have a soul of their own, something like Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She __was__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an __apothecary__ table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __wise__ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Has been"** would imply the search is ongoing, which contradicts the past tense narrative of the passage.
 
• **"Were"** is not suitable because the subject is singular, referring to "she," and we need the past tense form of the verb for a singular subject.
 
• **"Is"** would incorrectly place the sentence in the present tense, which doesn't fit with the rest of the passage's past tense structure.
